subject: Clarify minimum-billing vs atomic-unit accounting for short/interleaved calls
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@starlite.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: How are short, interleaved calls billed? Clarify minimums

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. One thing in our cost model that we need clarified before we can finalize an internal forecast: how Redwood charges for lots of very short, interleaved calls from our mobile app.

Example: a single user triggers 30 micro-requests per minute (each ~15–50 tokens of generated output). If you apply a per-call minimum (we've seen references to a 64-token floor elsewhere), the rounding kills our economics. Do you charge per-call atomic unit, per-user window, or do you aggregate by session/context to avoid repeated minimums?

Can you share the exact rules (minimum token floor, rounding direction, whether prefix reuse reduces billable units) and ideally a worked example for three short calls of 24/38/12 tokens?

I'll attach a sample usage CSV and our Q1 invoice for context.

Thanks,
-Alex
Alex Chen
Lead PM, Integrations
Starlite Health
Attachments: starlite_sample_usage.csv (csv), starlite_q1_invoice.pdf (pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@starlite.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-10T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: How are short, interleaved calls billed? Clarify minimums

Alex —

Really useful question; appreciate the concrete numbers. Short answer: default hosted billing is atomic-per-request with a configurable minimum per-request floor and a short-session aggregation window we can enable for pilots. I'll sketch the defaults and then propose a pilot concession.

Current default (hosted):
- Billing unit: per API call (atomic)
- Minimum floor: 48 tokens per completed generation (rounded up)
- Rounding: per-call rounding up to nearest whole token after tokenization; if call < floor, charged as floor
- Prefix/KV reuse: automatic KV/prefix caching reduces compute but does not alter tokenized length for billing unless you enable 'conversation rollup' which aggregates sequential calls into one billing event when calls are within the same session and share context.

Worked example (your three calls 24 / 38 / 12):
- With default atomic-floor=48: billed tokens = 48 + 48 + 48 = 144 tokens
- If conversation rollup is ON and the calls occur within a 2-minute window with shared context: billed tokens = tokenized length of combined inputs+outputs — for your numbers roughly 24+38+12 + small overhead = ~76 tokens (single floor still applies if final aggregate < floor)

Proposed pilot (for Starlite):
- Enable 2-minute aggregation window for mobile microcalls originating from the same user/session
- Soft-floor: charge max(real token sum, 32) per aggregated window (lower than default 48)
- Pilot concession: 10% discount on those aggregated windows for first quarter after go-live (to prove cost parity)

I copied Marissa (CS) to align on contract language and Neha (finance) for billing impact — Marissa, Neha, any comments before I formalize?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups:

1) If we take the pilot concession, how will we reflect that on the invoice? Will you show aggregated windows as a separate line item so we can reconcile against our event logs? We need line-level detail for our FinOps team.

2) Can the aggregation be limited to 'mobile microcalls' only (we still want full accounting for other paths)?

3) For the worked example, can you show the math including tokenization differences (we use a UTF-8 heavy payload so tokenization sometimes increases output token counts)?

Attaching the sample CSV and a redacted invoice — the invoice has monthly volumes so the pilot will materially change our forecast if we don't get the floor lowered.

Appreciate the quick attention.

-Alex

Karthik —

We can support this pilot but need a few guardrails to keep accounting clean:

1) Invoice line-level: yes — we will add a discrete invoice SKU 'AGG_MOBILE_MICRO' that reports three fields per line: raw_token_sum, applied_floor, post_discount_charge. That will let Starlite reconcile to their logs.

2) Tagging: we'll require the client to set an explicit request header x-rw-aggregation: mobile-micro to enable aggregation at the routing layer. Requests without the header will be billed under standard atomic rules.

3) Floor/discount: approve soft-floor=32 tokens, aggregation window 120s, pilot discount 10% for 90 days. After pilot we revert to default except we can negotiate a longer-term floor if volumes meet threshold.

4) Tokenization variance: we'll include a tokenization debug export for the pilot (sampled) so Starlite can see how our tokenizer maps their UTF-8 payloads. That should address the tokenization delta.

Operational notes:
- We need a signed addendum (I'll draft language) and a start/end date for the pilot. Billing team prefers the pilot billed monthly with a reconciliation report at month-end.
- Marketers: ensure CS collects a single point-of-contact on the Starlite side for troubleshooting tokenization mismatches.

Marissa — if you're comfortable with the customer experience side, I can produce the addendum and update the invoice template.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
